newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh and Vietnam have signed a trade agreement providing the "most favoured nation" status to each other to promote bilateral trade and economic cooperation.
A mild earthquake shook several northern districts on Tuesday. Panick-stricken residents in Rajshahi city rushed out of homes to open places, but there were no reports of casualty or damage.
Bangladesh Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad, now on a visit to USA, has urged the US government to waive outstanding debt amounting $739 million.

Retired army colonel Syed Farooq Rahman, charged with killing of four Awami League leaders in prison after 1975 military coup, was sent to jail on Tuesday after police interrogation for more than a month.

UN Under Secretary General Rafeeuddin Ahmed said Bangladesh needed to reform investment related laws to attract Foreign Direct Investment (FDI). FDI in Bangladesh rose from $11 million in 1994 to $125 million in 1995, but the flow is insignificant in global context, according to World Investment Report 1996 of UNCTAD released in Dhaka on Tuesday.

Bangladesh's imports from Asian countries grew faster in 1994-95 (July-June) than its exports. According to official figures, Bangladesh's export to its 20 Asian trading partners amounted to $466.24 million against import of $3.21 billion.
Four Bangladeshi shoe companies have received export order of 50,000 pairs of shoes from German firms during a recent international shoe fair in Germany.
